description: Blocks STARTING a heavy operation (VS Code extension rebuild/`vsce package`, a multi-model `review diff`/`quorum`/`brainstorm`/`just-ask` pass, or a build/test-suite run) while the machine's real memory pressure is at WARN-or-worse (macOS `sysctl kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` >= RIG_HEAVY_OP_BLOCK_AT_LEVEL, default 2; 1=normal/2=warn/4=critical — the same signal Activity Monitor's Memory Pressure graph and the OS's own OOM killer read, not a noisy raw free-byte count). Added after a 2026-08-27/28 incident where ~10-15 concurrent background agents running heavy local work (extension rebuilds, multi-model review passes, full test suites) drove free memory to ~65MB on a 24GB machine and hung several real VS Code windows. Deliberately stateless — no counter, no lock file, no queue — every invocation re-reads real pressure fresh, so nothing can leak a slot or deadlock a second hook; a retry after genuine memory frees up passes. No self-bypass and deliberately no Telegram hatch-escalation (this is an objective, self-resolving fact, not a human judgment call) — applies to BOTH the orchestrator and subagents (unlike the agent_id-gated hooks in this directory), since the failure mode was total-machine memory pressure regardless of which actor started the operation. Fails open (allows) when no reliable pressure signal is available (non-macOS without PSI, or the sysctl call itself fails) — this is an availability circuit-breaker, not a security boundary. on_error=open.
